jurisdiction.name: Uganda
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Uganda has no AI-specific law or strategy yet. AI is covered by the Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 (in force since 3 May 2019), which gives rights over automated decision-taking, and the 2020 National Fourth Industrial Revolution Strategy. In 2026 the National Information Technology Authority (NITA-U) issued two frameworks binding on public bodies, the National Information Security Policy and the e-Government Interoperability Framework, which require AI risk assessments, bias testing, explainability and human oversight. A 2025 national AI landscape assessment by the ICT ministry and the ITU feeds a National AI and Emerging Technologies Strategy that is still in consultation.
lead_institutions: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering Parliament, the ICT ministry, NITA-U's guidelines and laws pages, each line ministry and each sector regulator. The Uganda Gazette has no searchable online portal. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the data protection office, the health and justice ministries, the standards bureau and the revenue authority. The national AI strategy (its June 2026 target has passed with no text published), the 2021 data protection regulations, the Copyright (Amendment) Bill 2025 and the judiciary's use of AI are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: The Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
instruments.current_status: In force since 3 May 2019. The copy on the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance 'Acts and Laws' page is the assented Act (date of assent 25 February 2019 handwritten on the assent page). The official revised edition, published by NITA-U on its 'Laws and Regulations' page as the Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap. 97, states 'Commencement: 3 May, 2019' and keeps section 27 (rights in relation to automated decision-taking). Its implementing Data Protection and Privacy Regulations, 2021 and proposals to amend the Act to address AI are listed under Leads.
instruments.summary: Uganda's general data protection law, binding on public bodies and private data collectors, processors and controllers; it sets data protection principles, consent, purpose limitation, security and breach-notification duties, and creates the Personal Data Protection Office under the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (the 'Authority'). Section 27 gives data subjects rights in relation to automated decision-taking: they may require that significant decisions are not based solely on automated processing, must be notified when such a decision is taken, and may require reconsideration within 21 days, with complaints to the Authority. These provisions are the main existing legal rules applying to AI systems that process personal data in Uganda.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only enacted law with an explicit automated decision-making provision (s. 27); governs personal data used to train and run AI.
metadata_gaps: Uganda Gazette publication reference not located on an official site
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): 32-page scanned PDF of the assented Act read as page images (title page, assent page dated 25/2/2019, arrangement of sections, s. 2 definitions, ss. 25-28 incl. s. 27 automated decision-taking); re-checked 2026-10-13: assented PDF re-fetched by curl (HTTP 200); commencement date 3 May 2019 and s. 27 read in the revised edition Cap. 97 PDF on nita.go.ug (curl, pdftotext) Issuing act details: Parliament of Uganda (assented to by the President on 25 February 2019).

instruments.official_title: Uganda's National 4IR Strategy: A continental 4IR hub that enables a smart and connected Ugandan society (Executive Summary)
instruments.english_title: Uganda's National Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Strategy (Executive Summary)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, developed by the National Expert Taskforce on the Fourth Industrial Revolution established by the President in 2018
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
instruments.current_status: Only the executive summary is published on the Ministry's 'Strategies and Frameworks' page; the summary itself carries no date, and the year 2020 is taken from the Ministry/ITU 'Uganda national AI landscape assessment', which cites it as 'Uganda National 4IR Strategy, 2020'. It is the existing umbrella strategy for AI and other 4IR technologies; a dedicated National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy was under consultation in 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Uganda's national strategy for Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies, including AI, blockchain, IoT and cloud computing, prepared on the advice of the presidential National Expert Taskforce on the 4IR with the vision of a continental 4IR hub and a smart and connected Ugandan society. It identifies domain opportunities (e.g. AI diagnostics in health, AI-based tax compliance and agriculture applications) and five critical enablers: 4IR connectivity, agile governance, an upskilled population, eGovernment and local innovation. Under 'regulatory agility' it prioritises data legislation and regulation and calls for equipping regulators to respond quickly, allow experimentation with new technologies and close legislative and regulatory gaps created by 4IR technologies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current umbrella strategy covering AI; precursor to the National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy under development.
metadata_gaps: Exact publication or adoption date not stated on the document (year from the Ministry/ITU AI landscape assessment)
Full strategy text not published; only the executive summary

instruments.current_status: Published in 2025 (ITU copyright 2025, ISBN 978-92-61-40291-4) and listed on the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance 'Reports' page, with a foreword by the Minister of ICT and National Guidance. Its recommendations (AI policy, strategy and legal framework) feed the National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy under development.
instruments.summary: Government assessment of Uganda's AI readiness, prepared by the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance with ITU through a baseline survey of public and private AI actors, stakeholder consultations, benchmarking against Rwanda, Kenya and the United States, and an assessment of government infrastructure and skills for AI-enabled e-services. It finds gaps in AI infrastructure, skills, curricula and the absence of an AI policy, legal and regulatory framework. It proposes an AI risk management framework (risk matrix, legal and standards-based approaches, governance, risk identification, assessment, monitoring and reporting) and recommends that the Government develop an AI policy, strategy and legal and regulatory framework, invest in high-performance computing and use public-private partnerships.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Official AI readiness assessment with a proposed national AI risk management framework; basis for the forthcoming AI strategy.

instruments.official_title: National Information Security Framework (NISF): National Information Security Policy (NISP) 2026
instruments.english_title: National Information Security Framework (NISF) – National Information Security Policy (NISP) 2026
instruments.issuing_authority: National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (NITA-U); launched by the Minister of ICT and National Guidance
instruments.current_status: Launched on 15 July 2026 by the Minister of ICT and National Guidance at an event hosted by NITA-U under the UDAP-GovNet project (NITA-U news page). It updates the 2014 National Information Security Framework; the document states that the policy is mandatory for all public and private organisations that use, own or operate protected computers, critical information infrastructure, official communications systems or personal data processing environments. No separate commencement date is stated.
instruments.summary: Uganda's updated national information security policy and framework, setting mandatory minimum security requirements for Ministries, Departments and Agencies, Local Governments, critical information infrastructure operators and other entities processing national information, aligned with ISO/IEC 27001/27002, NIST CSF and national laws. Its control section 5.2.4.3 on Artificial Intelligence requires organisations to carry out initial and ongoing AI risk assessments covering privacy, bias, fairness and explainability, audit AI systems for emerging ethical risks, comply with the Data Protection and Privacy Act (with DPIAs) when AI processes personal data, protect models and training data against poisoning and leakage, perform adversarial testing and performance monitoring, keep high-impact AI decisions auditable and transparent, and maintain human oversight of AI-driven critical decisions. It also defines an AI Security/Controller role with ISO/IEC 23894-related competences.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding-in-scope national instrument with AI-specific security, risk and human-oversight controls.
metadata_gaps: No commencement date stated in the document
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext): preface, version history, s. 1.2 applicability (mandatory), s. 5.2.4.3 Artificial Intelligence controls and AI Security/Controller role; launch date 15 July 2026 from the NITA-U news page 'Hon. Lumumba launches updated National Information Security Framework (NISF) 2026' and the Ministry of ICT news item of 16 July 2026

instruments.current_status: Second version of the national e-GIF, dated 15 April 2026 on its cover and published on NITA-U's 'Guidelines & IT standards' page with its companion reference architecture (GIRA-2026). It builds on and replaces e-GIF-2021 (not recorded). The document states it is mandatory for all Ministries, Departments, Agencies and Local Governments; no launch notice or commencement date was found.
instruments.summary: Mandatory interoperability framework for all Ugandan Ministries, Departments, Agencies and Local Governments, with which all digital initiatives, procurement and system developments must conform. It sets principles for AI in public administration: AI as an additive layer that systems must be able to run without, a mandatory human review 'break point' for critical processes, full traceability before automation, and bounded delegation for autonomous agents, plus an ethics-by-design approach requiring explainable and auditable AI-assisted decisions affecting citizens' rights, mandatory human-in-the-loop for complex decision support, and bias testing. It also calls for clarifying the legal bases for automated and AI-assisted decisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sets binding-in-scope AI principles (human oversight, transparency, bias testing) for government systems.
metadata_gaps: Date is the cover date of the document; no launch notice found

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Uganda's gazette, Parliament, the ICT ministry, the national IT authority, each ministry and sector regulators were searched. No qualifying document was found for procurement, standards, sandboxes, sector-specific rules, generative AI, drafts, international agreements or historical publications. Several official sites, including Parliament's bill pages, the data protection office, the health and justice ministries, the standards bureau and the central bank's circulars, were unavailable, so the 2021 data protection regulations, a 2025 copyright amendment bill and other reported documents still need to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one).
